# ---- Memory ----
# The NPDM declares 48 MiB of system resources. Startup requests a 6.20 GiB heap.
# The alias region holds the game's streaming allocator (main+0x7ed630): in Kokiri Forest it keeps about 5,100 address regions with 3.0-3.3 GB mapped, spread up to
# +4.95 GB (DM_REGIONS). With 2.38 GB (0x98000000) VammManager::AllocateAddressRegion failed after 5-15 minutes outdoors and the game aborted (nn::diag abort,
# Result 0, sdk+0x16cb54). 8 GB leaves room for its fragmentation; the reserve grows by the same 5.6 GB so the heap keeps its size
mem_reserve
mem_alias
# A map that would take the process past the application pool fails with ResultLimitReached, as on Horizon: the SDK's allocator keeps freed pages mapped until a map fails,
# then gives them back. Without it PR #1444 reports crashes entering Hyrule Castle, Kakariko Village and Death Mountain and a black screen leaving the Deku Tree
mem_map_limit
mem_stack
app_pool
sys_resource
# ---- Shader split ----
shader_groups
shader_note
# Mac shader libraries without fast math (dmsh_build.py SHADER_MATH): with fast or relaxed maths single grass blades went pure white for a frame (Hyrule Field, the castle moat)
shader_math
# ---- Frame rate ----
# The game steps its time by a frame ratio, its base rate / its frame rate, whatever the frame took: frames longer than a vsync played in slow motion. The ratio takes the host's
# frame step instead (MATCH_FRAME_STEP in patches.py, found by its function on any build that keeps it): 1 vsync at 60 fps, 2 when 60 does not hold, so game time = real time
# (frames that are not whole vsyncs long: the stub takes the measured frame time when it is longer than that step, DM_FRAME_DELTA=0 turns that off)
fps_target
# ---- Graphics ----
# agl wraps its depth clears in render conditions, as on Donkey Kong Bananza and Splatoon Raiders: in Kokiri Forest the main opaque pass tests EQUAL against a copy of the prepass depth
# that a conditional clear (skipped on the console) wiped first, so no lit geometry landed and the full-screen sky showed through everywhere (a white scene)
render_cond

# The game turns the difference of two raw counter reports into its wind and particle time step at the Switch 2's system counter rate. At NVN's 614.4 MHz the step was 19.66 times too large: foliage, leaves and hanging plants moved about 20 times too fast
gpu_ts_hz
# Pool tables (shaders reading textures through handles cover every registered ID, about 33,000) made a texture again for each ID whose texture the game had finalized: at the
# house-to-forest change 1,500 textures and 2.5 GB held only by retired IDs, as much again in deferred release, 16 GB GPU allocated and out of GPU memory. Retired IDs get the dummy
pool_skip_retired
# Guest copies of textures in CPU_NO_ACCESS pools (render and depth targets the game cannot read) given back once their GPU copy exists (upstream #1447, nvn_mtl.m rel_*): about 550 MB outdoors.
# Level 1 since V23. Level 2 (also CPU-visible copies, pages unwritten since their upload) saved 1.85 GB more in Kokiri Forest (peak 7.0 → 5.2 GB with the iPhone's guest files),
# but a texture the game makes again over released pages reads zeros: magenta and black ground, cliffs, walls and doors after area changes (Kokiri Forest, Hyrule Field, Hyrule Castle).
# Upstream #1641 and #1972 (both on this fork) found level 1 fixes it. DM_TEX_RELEASE=2 brings the saving back
tex_release
# Large block-compressed textures from the game files kept without their finest level on the GPU (tex_soft, ported from the plumber-racer-2 fork)
tex_soft
# rt_drop (render targets taken over by a later-drawn one become 1x1 stand-ins, nvn_mtl.m rtd_sweep) is off: footprint 8.9 → 7.1 GB at the Kokiri Forest doorway, but the game still
# samples textures the sweep took for dead (on the title screen 278 of about 300 stand-ins were drawn again): textures and objects popped on and off, surfaces swayed and some were missing
rt_drop
# Handheld, as the iPhone runs it (the game presents 1920x1080 instead of 2048x1152 docked)
op_mode
# Render pipelines through Metal 4 on the iPhone too, as on the Mac: the pipeline archive and hybrid pipelines (a draw starts with a ready base instead of waiting for its own pipeline).
# With it off, every pipeline the game first used compiled on the submit thread: on an iPhone 18 Pro the opening cutscene's transitions froze for 0.2-1.3 s each. Since X3 the IPA
# carries the offline archive for the A20 (pso_gpu below); the launcher's pipeline prebuild builds on the device whatever it does not hold
pso_mtl4
# The pipeline archive made offline for the iPhone 18 Pro's GPU (applegpu_g19p, the architecture its logs name), so draws start from ready bases (hybrid pipelines) instead of
# compiling at their first draw: X2 at 30 fps froze 0.3-2.9 s at new areas and effects (log 70: 45 pipelines in one 2.86 s frame, archive lookups found 0, hybrid draws 0). Until X3, every V and X
# build used --gpu none, as the A20's architecture name was not known
pso_gpu
# no payback: a late frame's lost time is let go (the game slows by it, as on the console) instead of a step of 3 vsyncs shown for 2, a half-frame jump in motion on the next frame
fps_payback
# The iPhone's touch gamepad starts in the full (3D) layout: the D-pad, L3 / R3 and the right stick, which turns the camera (a drag in the right third of the screen); the simple
# layout has no right stick. A layout the player switches to in the game menu is kept
# The launcher's Potato mode (DM_PRESET=potato; loader.c dm_preset_apply sets this list when the game starts): the A line's memory savers, for iPhones with less memory. An iPhone 15
# Pro (A17 Pro, 8 GB) gives the game about 6.0 GB, against 8.0 on an iPhone 18 Pro, and was ended by the system at the load after the opening cutscene (GPU allocated 2.8 → 7.0 GB in
# 20 s). With Potato mode off none of these runs. The GPU memory guard lets go from 4,400 MB; a 64 MB texture recycle bin; shared textures nothing looked up for 600 fences swept; the
# prewarm keeps no pipeline (warm-only, in the background); pools over 512 MB stay in the guest files, wired by the chunks the GPU reaches; render and depth targets of 4 MB and more
# made only when a draw binds them (lazy textures). The Render scale stays the player's
potato
# Dynamic resolution reads the GPU time between the frame's timestamp reports, as on Donkey Kong Bananza and Breath of the Wild (the same EPD engine family): with one time a submission it
# read about 0 and kept the full 1440x810 at 20-24 ms of GPU a frame on a MacBook Air M5. Each report takes its segment's GPU start / end (nvn_mtl.m rep_ticks)
gpu_timestamps

# The game upscales through a chain: agl_ndsr_vr feature pass, network and blend at the render size, agl_ndsr_vr_light scale to 1920x1080. DM_UPSCALER=metalfx skips the chain for MetalFX (nvn_mtl.m up_chain)
upscaler_chain
# Colour render targets drawn only as attachments (RGBA8 / BGRA8 / RGBA16F) kept with Metal lossy compression (rt_lossy, nvn_mtl.m rt_lossy): about 100 MB less in Link's house at 720p;
# the scene colour (RG11B10F) and depth have no lossy form
rt_lossy
# The game's compute dispatches with no barrier of its between them run side by side (nvn_mtl.m dispatch_enc): 117 at the start of a frame in Kokiri Forest waited each for the one
# before, 5.7 ms; side by side 3.7 ms, the frame 27.1 -> 24.9 ms (docked, Apple M4 Pro), the picture within run-to-run noise
dispatch_overlap
# The indirect dispatch clamp off: walking through Hyrule Castle Town, 6-9 long frames in 47 s with it off against 13-24 with it on (an extra dispatch and barrier before each
# indirect dispatch; docked, render scale 1.0, Apple M4 Pro), and no indirect dispatch of this game has hung the GPU. DM_NVN_DISPATCH_CLAMP=1 turns it back on
dispatch_clamp
# The terrain tiles' height, blend and hole maps (260x260, one CPU_CACHED | GPU_CACHED pool) are rewritten from the CPU with no flush as tile slots are reused: without these the
# tiles kept what they held before, flat blue and grey holes in the ground with the grass drawn over them (Kokiri Forest, the Lost Woods)
tex_flush_upload
tex_dirty_upload
# Touch controls from cheemu21/kid-with-sword-remake: the Native layout (a mobile game's layout in very transparent glass) in the Forest colours; DM_PAD_THEME=0 in env.txt gives the Classic colours
pad_layout
pad_theme
# cheemu21 V17, a steady 30 fps (frame generation): present snapshots, display-link frame latency 2 at the 30 fps cap (frame buffering: a 34-38 ms frame is absorbed),
# and no payback step (a late frame's lost time is let go instead of a step of 3 vsyncs shown for 2, a half-frame jump)
present_snap
link_latency30
# The game submits a frame's commands behind an event its CPU signals once the frame before has left the GPU, so the GPU starts each frame with nothing queued and waits for the
# replay: with Metal encoding on its own thread a GPU-bound Hyrule Field scene went 55.3-55.8 -> 56.5-56.9 fps (Apple M4 Pro, three runs a side, interleaved)
enc_thread
